description: BBHT runs Grover search when the number of marked states is not known. Each round picks an iteration count `j` uniformly below a bound `m`, applies `j` Grover iterations, measures and checks the measured candidate, for `j + 1` queries. After a failed round the bound grows by a factor of `6/5`, inside the paper's `1 < λ < 4/3`, from 1 up to `√N`. The search stops at the first candidate that passes the check, or when the call has spent its query budget, cutting the last round short to fit; a returned index is always marked, but no result can also mean that the budget was too small. The expected cost is `O(√(N/M))` queries for `M` of `N` states marked, and a budget of `9·(⌊√N⌋ + 1)` makes a miss rare; use it when you do not know how many solutions exist.

papers.authors: Michel Boyer, Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Alain Tapp
papers.title: Tight Bounds on Quantum Searching

lineage.source: quantum-planning, src/grover/bbht.rs: "Runs Grover search without a known marked count and returns a verified index."
